Aqeedah means belief: what a Muslim hold: Aqeedah means belief: what a Muslim holds to be true in the heart. Every Muslim who has reached adulthood and is sane must know what is necessary for Allah, what is impossible for Him, and what is possible for Him, and the same for the Messengers عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ.
Look at the world: things move then stop: Look at the world: things move then stop, grow then fade, arrive then leave. Each new state had a beginning. Imam al-Sanusi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says something that is never free of changes that begin must itself have begun. So the world came into being; it has not always been there.
Allah has no end (baqa'). He will never: Allah has no end (baqa'). He will never cease to be. As Imam al-Tahawi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says: He is Eternal without a beginning and Everlasting without an end.
The Maturidis, the school of Imam Abu Ma: The Maturidis, the school of Imam Abu Mansur al-Maturidi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ followed by most Hanafis, add an eighth attribute of meaning: takwin, Allah's bringing things into being. The Ash'aris count this under power and will. Both schools are Ahl al-Sunnah.
Imam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله said: the Qur: Imam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ said: the Qur'an is written in the copies, preserved in the hearts and recited by the tongues. Our pronouncing, writing and reciting it are created; the Qur'an itself is not created.
He ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets. 'Isa ع: He ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets. 'Isa عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ will return, but as a follower of his law.
Allah took Ibrahim عليه السلام as His cl: Allah took Ibrahim عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ as His close friend and spoke to Musa عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ directly. Muhammad ﷺ is the Seal of the Prophets and the master of the Messengers.
Imam al-Tahawi رحمه الله says the meanin: Imam al-Tahawi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ says the meaning of seeing Allah is as Allah intended and knows. The sound hadith say the believers will see their Lord as clearly as the full moon. We accept these as the Prophet ﷺ said them, without picturing how and without comparing Allah to creation.
The Hour is the Day of Judgement. Before: The Hour is the Day of Judgement. Before it comes there are signs. Among the great signs Imam al-Tahawi mentions: the coming of the Dajjal (the great deceiver), and 'Isa ibn Maryam عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ coming down from the sky.
'Isa عليه السلام coming down from the sk: 'Isa عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ coming down from the sky
We do not prefer any wali to any Prophet: We do not prefer any wali to any Prophet عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ. One Prophet is better than all the awliya' together.
This course follows the Hanafi school of: This course follows the Hanafi school of Imam Abu Hanifah al-Nu'man رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, through Nur al-Idah of Imam al-Shurunbulali رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ and Mukhtasar al-Quduri of Imam al-Quduri رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ.
Imam al-Ghazali رحمه الله opens this boo: Imam al-Ghazali رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ opens this book with the virtue of the lawful and the blame of the unlawful, bringing verses and hadiths on how what we consume affects our worship.
Imam al-Ghazali رحمه الله wrote that dou: Imam al-Ghazali رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ wrote that doubt overcame him so strongly that for nearly two months he could not trust even the basic truths of the mind.
Al-Ghazali quotes 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رضي: Al-Ghazali quotes 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: 'Do not know the truth by men. Know the truth, and you will know its people.'
'Ali ibn Abi Talib رضي الله عنه: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
Al-Ghazali quotes it from 'Ali رضي الله: Al-Ghazali quotes it from 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.
Muhammad ﷺ, son of 'Abdullah, son of 'Ab: Muhammad ﷺ, son of 'Abdullah, son of 'Abd al-Muttalib, son of Hashim, of Quraysh, from the descendants of Isma'il عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ.
At twelve his uncle Abu Talib took him o: At twelve his uncle Abu Talib took him on a trade journey to Syria. Later he travelled there again trading for Khadijah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا.
He ﷺ migrated with Abu Bakr رضي الله عنه: He ﷺ migrated with Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, hiding in the cave of Thawr, then reached Quba' and Madinah, built the masjid and joined the Muhajirun and Ansar in brotherhood.
At Uhud the archers left their post agai: At Uhud the archers left their post against the Prophet's ﷺ order, and the Muslims suffered. Hamzah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ was martyred.
All his children were from Khadijah رضي: All his children were from Khadijah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا except Ibrahim, from Mariyah. They were al-Qasim (his kunyah Abu al-Qasim is from him), Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, Fatimah, 'Abdullah and Ibrahim.
All of his children died before him exce: All of his children died before him except Fatimah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا, who passed away a few months after him.
His first wife was Khadijah رضي الله عنه: His first wife was Khadijah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا, the first to believe in him. He married no one else in her lifetime.
Anas رضي الله عنه described him ﷺ: neith: Anas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ described him ﷺ: neither very tall nor short, neither very white nor dark, his hair neither tightly curled nor straight.
Anas رضي الله عنه served him for ten yea: Anas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ served him for ten years, and he ﷺ never once said 'uff' to him, nor asked 'why did you do that?'
'A'ishah رضي الله عنها was asked about h: 'A'ishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا was asked about his character. She said: 'His character was the Qur'an.'
'A'ishah رضي الله عنها said she saw reve: 'A'ishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا said she saw revelation come to him on a very cold day, and when it left him his forehead was dripping with sweat.
Jibril عليه السلام met the Prophet ﷺ eve: Jibril عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ met the Prophet ﷺ every night of Ramadan and studied the Qur'an with him.
After many reciters were martyred at Yam: After many reciters were martyred at Yamamah, 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ urged Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ to collect the Qur'an. Abu Bakr gave the task to Zayd ibn Thabit رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ, a scribe of revelation.
Zayd gathered it from palm stalks, flat: Zayd gathered it from palm stalks, flat stones and the memories of men. The sheets stayed with Abu Bakr, then 'Umar, then Hafsah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ.
When Hudhayfah رضي الله عنه saw people d: When Hudhayfah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ saw people differing in recitation, 'Uthman رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ had copies made from Hafsah's sheets and sent one to each region.
Zayd ibn Thabit رضي الله عنه: Zayd ibn Thabit رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
'Umar رضي الله عنه heard Hisham ibn Haki: 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ heard Hisham ibn Hakim رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ recite differently and brought him to the Prophet ﷺ, who approved both and said the Qur'an was revealed in seven modes (ahruf).
The Qur'an is preserved in hearts as wel: The Qur'an is preserved in hearts as well as written in copies, as Imam Abu Hanifah رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ said. Every generation has had countless people who memorised it.
Imam al-Ghazali رحمه الله begins by aski: Imam al-Ghazali رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ begins by asking why you seek knowledge. If it is to compete, show off and win people's attention, you are tearing down your religion. If it is for guidance, the angels spread their wings for you as you walk.
Short du'as the Prophet ﷺ taught for eve: Short du'as the Prophet ﷺ taught for everyday moments. Imam al-Nawawi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ (d. 676 AH), the great hadith scholar, gathered them with their sources in his book al-Adhkar. Learn one at a time and say it each time that moment comes.

Abu Dawud and Ibn al-Sunni (272), from M: Abu Dawud and Ibn al-Sunni (272), from Mu'adh ibn Anas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ; al-Nawawi, al-Adhkar
Abu Dawud (5095) and al-Tirmidhi (3426),: Abu Dawud (5095) and al-Tirmidhi (3426), from Anas رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ; al-Nawawi, al-Adhkar
Abu Dawud, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari رضي: Abu Dawud, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ; al-Nawawi, al-Adhkar

al-Bukhari (5743) and Muslim (2191), fro: al-Bukhari (5743) and Muslim (2191), from 'A'ishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا; al-Nawawi, al-Adhkar
Sahih Muslim (2202), from 'Uthman ibn Ab: Sahih Muslim (2202), from 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'As رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ; al-Nawawi, al-Adhkar
Sahih al-Bukhari (1032), from 'A'ishah ر: Sahih al-Bukhari (1032), from 'A'ishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا; al-Nawawi, al-Adhkar
al-Tirmidhi (3451), from Talhah رضي الله: al-Tirmidhi (3451), from Talhah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ; al-Nawawi, al-Adhkar
Ibn al-Sunni, from 'Ali رضي الله عنه; al: Ibn al-Sunni, from 'Ali رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ; al-Nawawi, al-Adhkar

Forty du'as from the Qur'an that begin ر: Forty du'as from the Qur'an that begin رَبُّنَا, 'Our Lord'. They are the words of the prophets عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ and the believers, which Allah kept in His Book. Many people read all forty after a prayer, or one a day.

Imam Abu Hamid al-Ghazali رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ (d. 505 AH) is called Hujjat al-Islam, 'the Proof of Islam'. He was a Shafi'i jurist, an Ash'ari theologian and a Sufi master. In his short book Bidayat al-Hidayah ('The Beginning of Guidance') he walks a beginner through one day of worship. These are the du'as he teaches for each part of that day, in his own words.
We have entered the morning and the domi: We have entered the morning and the dominion belongs to Allah; greatness and authority, might and power belong to Allah, Lord of the worlds. We have entered the morning upon the natural way of Islam, the word of sincerity, the religion of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and the way of our father Ibrahim عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ, upright and submitting, who was not of the idolaters.
Al-Ghazali recommends these. Imam al-Naw: Al-Ghazali recommends these. Imam al-Nawawi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ notes in al-Adhkar that the limb-by-limb du'as are not reported from the Prophet ﷺ; they are good words of du'a, said without believing them to be a sunnah. Your wudu is complete without them.
Hands on the thighs. Recite the tashahhu: Hands on the thighs. Recite the tashahhud of Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ.
Mukhtasar al-Quduri, how to pray; Sahih: Mukhtasar al-Quduri, how to pray; Sahih al-Bukhari (831) and Muslim (402), from Ibn Mas'ud رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

Related by Imam al-Fakihani رحمه الله (d: Related by Imam al-Fakihani رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ (d. 734 AH) in al-Fajr al-Munir, from Shaykh Musa al-Darir رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ, who was taught it in a dream of the Prophet ﷺ when his ship was caught in a storm; he and the passengers recited it and the storm passed. Al-Sakhawi also mentions it.
Attributed to Shaykh Ibrahim al-Tazi رحم: Attributed to Shaykh Ibrahim al-Tazi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ (d. 866 AH) of the Maghrib.
Composed by Shaykh Muhammad ibn Abi al-H: Composed by Shaykh Muhammad ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Bakri رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ (d. 952 AH) of Egypt; recited widely, especially in the Tijani path.
Attributed to Shaykh Abu Bakr ibn Salim: Attributed to Shaykh Abu Bakr ibn Salim al-'Alawi رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ (d. 992 AH) of Hadramawt, and widely recited in the Indian subcontinent.
Attributed in devotional books to Sayyid: Attributed in devotional books to Sayyiduna al-Khidr عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ; no chain is known for this.
Durood Lakhi (said in devotional manuals: Durood Lakhi (said in devotional manuals to equal 100,000 salawat — a virtue not found in the hadith collections) and Dala'il al-Khayrat of Imam al-Jazuli رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ will be added once we have a verified printed text to copy from, so that not a letter is wrong.

Imam Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Jazuli رحم: Imam Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Jazuli رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ (d. 870 AH)
This is the description of the blessed g: This is the description of the blessed garden in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is buried, with his two companions Abu Bakr and 'Umar رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا.
So it was described by 'Urwah ibn al-Zub: So it was described by 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was buried in the alcove, Abu Bakr رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ was buried behind him, and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ at the feet of Abu Bakr. The eastern part of the alcove remained empty, with room for a grave. It is said, and Allah knows best, that 'Isa son of Maryam عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ will be buried there, and so it has come in a report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
'A'ishah رضي الله عنها said: I saw three: 'A'ishah رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا said: I saw three moons fall into my room, and told my dream to Abu Bakr. He said: 'A'ishah, three people will be buried in your house who are the best of the people of the earth. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed away and was buried in my house, Abu Bakr said to me: This is one of your moons, and he is the best of them. Allah's abundant blessings and peace be on him and his family.
